review.title: The in-memory store is two stores: server components and route handlers never share one
review.acceptance: On a build with no DATABASE_URL, a row written through /api/v1/* is visible to a server component and the reverse, in the same process. REQUIRED: the continue-watching rail renders a title whose progress was written through the progress API -- which it does not today, silently. REQUIRED: /watchlist renders an entry added through the watchlist API. REQUIRED: the e2e coverage that watchlist.spec.ts currently skips with a stated reason on a development build is enabled by this task rather than deleted, and PW-0305's rail gains the equivalent. REQUIRED: whatever identity the fix uses must be justified against the alternative of declaring the in-memory adapter route-handler-only, which is a product decision rather than a refactor and would delete the list and the rail as currently designed.
review.notes: DEFECT, PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 100. Found while building PW-0304 and REPRODUCED TWICE on a running server; the full reproduction, including the one for PW-0305's rail, is the `defect.found` event of 2026-10-01. In one line: `lib/db/index.ts` caches the resolution in a module-level binding and `in-memory-repository.ts` builds its Maps at construction, and Next's app router compiles the React Server Components graph and the route-handler graph separately, so each gets its own store. PostgreSQL is unaffected, which is why it has been invisible. Created unowned so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict -- the remedy touches PW-0305's allowedPaths and the choice between fixing the identity and narrowing the adapter's contract is gpt-architect's to make.

typecheck.evidence:
`npm run typecheck` (turbo run typecheck): Tasks 22 successful, 22 total, exit 0. Also run directly
as `npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/web/tsconfig.json`, exit 0, and `npx tsc --noEmit` in `e2e/` (outside
the workspaces and therefore outside turbo's graph), exit 0 -- the new
`e2e/tests/continue-watching.spec.ts` is typechecked by the second of those and by nothing else.

The symbol-keyed property needs no `any`: the global is reached through one narrow interface
(`{ [STORE_SLOT]?: InMemoryStore }`) and a single `as unknown as` at the boundary, so every read
and write of the slot is typed.

unit.evidence:
`npm run test` (turbo run test): Tasks 22 successful, 22 total, exit 0. `apps/web` alone is 80 test
files / 1399 tests passed; `src/lib/db/` alone is 3 files / 61 tests.

WHAT THE NEW CASES COVER, against gpt-architect's round-101 evidence list.

in-memory-repository.test.ts, "the process store (PW-0313)" -- 7 cases:
  - the same store is handed to every caller in one realm;
  - a write through a repository built the way one Next graph builds it is READ through a
    separately-constructed one (items 1 and 2, as near as a unit test can get: it cannot build two
    Next module graphs, and says so);
  - the same in the reverse direction (item 3);
  - `createInMemoryRepository` still DEFAULTS to a fresh store, so no existing suite becomes
    order-dependent -- the sharing is a property of the composition root only;
  - the reset throws the store away, the next ask builds a new one, and the OLD object is left
    coherent rather than emptied;
  - ITEM 6, IN A REAL SECOND PROCESS: two `execFileSync(process.execPath, ["-e", ...])` children
    each write the slot and each report the slot was `absent` on entry. The child program
    interpolates `IN_MEMORY_STORE_GLOBAL_KEY`, the exported constant, so a rename cannot leave this
    test checking a stale literal;
  - a source rule that the module touches no `node:fs`, `node:path`, `localStorage` or
    `writeFile`, with a non-vacuity check -- the ruling says "do not persist this data to disk
    merely to solve module identity".

index.test.ts, "the in-memory branch resolves one store per process (PW-0313)" -- 3 cases:
  - two independent `selectRepository` calls (NOT `resolveRepository`, whose cache would hand back
    one object and make the test pass without sharing anything) produce two DIFFERENT repository
    objects that share state;
  - what they share is the store the module publishes, asserted against `processInMemoryStore()`
    rather than merely against each other -- otherwise two copies of the module could both be
    isolated and the suite still green;
  - the PostgreSQL branch is untouched: it still reports `postgres`, still returns a handle, and
    puts nothing in the process store.

ITEM 7, ISOLATION, IS EXPLICIT IN BOTH FILES: `beforeEach` and `afterEach` both call
`resetProcessInMemoryStore()`. The two hooks are not redundant -- the first protects the suite from
the world, the second protects the world from the suite, since any test anywhere that reaches
`selectRepository`'s in-memory branch now shares a store.

NON-VACUITY, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. With the one-line change in `index.ts` reverted --
`createInMemoryRepository(environment)` instead of
`createInMemoryRepository(environment, processInMemoryStore())` -- `src/lib/db/index.test.ts` goes
2 failed / 18 passed. The two that fail are the two that are about sharing; the PostgreSQL case
still passes, which is the point of having it.

e2e.evidence:
EXECUTED on bedceb5 plus this round's test changes. Browser: Chrome for Testing 151.0.7922.34,
revision 1234 -- the build @playwright/test 1.62.1 pins, resolved from /root/.cache/ms-playwright.
The container's PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH points at a 1194 tree which was NOT used.

WHOLE PROJECTS, NO SPEC FILTER, three configurations, exit 0 in each:

  development (in-memory, development-header identity), LIBERTY_E2E_PORT=3177
     --project=chromium : 27 passed,  6 skipped
     --project=api      : 55 passed,  8 skipped
  production + REAL POSTGRESQL 16.15, LIBERTY_E2E_PORT=3200,
  LIBERTY_E2E_DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:5433/lib_wl
     --project=chromium --project=api : 72 passed, 24 skipped

EVIDENCE ITEM 4 -- PW-0305's RAIL. `e2e/tests/continue-watching.spec.ts`, new, 4 cases: a profile
that has watched nothing gets no rail AND still gets the browse rails (the precondition that makes
the positive case mean something, since before this fix the rail was absent in every case); a
progress row written through the API is on the page; the card is the RESUME rendering of
`CatalogCard`, carrying the spoken "N% watched" and a start-over LINK with `?restart=1`; and one
household's resume point is not another's, which is the first question to ask of a store that just
became process-global.

EVIDENCE ITEM 5 -- THE DEVELOPMENT WATCHLIST PATH, ENABLED AND NOT DELETED, which is the wording of
gpt-architect's round-102 ruling. Four assertions were added to the development group of
`watchlist.spec.ts`, each marked PW-0313 in the source, each previously impossible:
  - after adding from a title page, `/watchlist` shows the title -- and NOT "Choose who is
    watching", which is what that page used to answer for a session that had plainly selected a
    profile;
  - after removing, `/watchlist` shows the empty panel and not the title;
  - after adding from a catalog card on the home screen, `/watchlist` shows that one title and not
    the other demo series -- the full journey through the UI, which no configuration could do
    before;
  - after a REFUSED write, `/watchlist` read back as the original identity is empty. That is the
    acceptance's "a refused write must not render as a success", checked in the one place a viewer
    would go to find out whether it worked.
The wire-level `listedContentIds` checks were NOT replaced. "The server agrees with the row" and
"the page agrees with the server" are different claims.

NON-VACUITY, MEASURED. With the one line in `lib/db/index.ts` reverted to
`createInMemoryRepository(environment)`, `watchlist.spec.ts` + `continue-watching.spec.ts` on
chromium/development go to 7 FAILED / 4 passed / 4 skipped: all four new watchlist page assertions
and three of the four continue-watching cases. Restored, the same two specs are 11 passed / 4
skipped, exit 0. Every assertion this gate rests on depends on the fix.

ONE EXISTING TEST WAS REPAIRED ON THE WAY, DISCLOSED RATHER THAN QUIETLY FIXED.
`critical-journey.spec.ts`'s play-affordance case failed at 12.0s with
`expect(page).toHaveURL` -- not a product failure: the click had navigated and the RSC request was
waiting on Turbopack's FIRST compile of `/watch/[contentId]`, which pulls shaka-player. The server
log straddles the failure ("Compiling /watch/[contentId] ..." then the failure then "200 in
262ms"), and the previous round's run logged the same compile at 6.8s and passed with under two
seconds of margin. This round's additions consumed that margin. Repaired by waiting on the
NAVIGATION (`page.waitForURL`) and keeping the URL assertion after it, so the wait is bounded by
the thing that actually varies. No timeout was raised and `retries` is still 0 -- PL-0706's
acceptance says raising a ceiling "moves the ceiling without removing the dependence". Diagnosis
recorded as `defect.found`.

WHAT THIS GATE STILL DOES NOT COVER. webkit, firefox and mobile-safari were not executed -- only
chromium 1234 is installed here. No configuration in this harness has both a real database and a
catalog, so the PostgreSQL run exercises the list page's `item: null` branch while the development
run exercises the named-card branch; between them both branches are covered, but not both on one
build. Nothing here ran on Windows and nothing here claims anything about Windows.
